notes: alpha = pressure / Fermi pressure at the same density (cold-fuel adiabat); NIF-class implosions run alpha 1.5-3
a finite temperature adds 3/2 n_i kT for the ions (ions are not degenerate) and raises the electron term; both are inside alpha here
the gate value (Lindl DT scaling by electrons per amu^(5/3)) agrees with the first-principles electron gas within the percentage given; exchange and lattice terms lower it by a few per cent

density_chain.note: E_comp = alpha K rho^(2/3) m and rho^(2/3) = rhoR (4 pi / 3 m)^(1/3): at fixed rhoR the compression energy grows as m^(2/3) while the yield grows as m, so gain rises only as m^(1/3)

DT_assisted.note: tritium decays (12.3 y) and the world inventory is tens of kg; on-board breeding needs a lithium blanket in a 14 MeV neutron flux, which is the opposite of the D-3He premise

operating_map.eta_c_literature_note: driver-to-fuel coupling: NIF indirect drive is about 1 % laser-to-fuel; direct-drive rocket (hydrodynamic) efficiency 5-15 %; heavy-ion direct-drive designs quote 10-20 %. These are literature ranges, not computed here.

gain_sensitivity_fdp1_V4.note: FDP-1 V4 alone (no coupled extras); departure mass rises steeply toward the threshold (83 kt at 842, 1.4 Mt at 703); the coupled extras raise the threshold

coupling_needed_for_closure.note: eta_c = G_threshold x alpha x E_comp / yield with a free ignitor: the smallest driver-to-fuel coupling at which this target could close the V4 ship at all

inert_mass.note: at fixed pulse energy an inert mass x times the fuel lowers ve by 1/sqrt(1+x); ln(mass ratio) grows by the inverse. x 0.76 is the Rev 4 HDC wall, x 2.6 a range-matched 0.12 mm HDC ablator (gate target.py)
